steps.name: QC and confounding diagnosis
caveats: Any PC1 separation between the two groups is uninterpretable in isolation: it is treatment + batch, and the data hold no information to split them.
12,000 rows is a pre-filtered or subset gene space, not a full transcriptome — do not describe it as genome-wide coverage.
steps.context: Raw integer gene-level counts from salmon, human lung, 6 treated vs 6 control. The data profile records that processing batch is perfectly confounded with condition. This step exists to document that confounding with data rather than assert it, and to catch any outlier sample before modelling.
steps.question: Do the 12 lung samples separate by condition (treated vs control), and can that separation be distinguished from the B1/B2 processing batch at all?

grounding.reason: Raw counts with 6 v 6 replicates: blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a sample distance heatmap coloured by condition and batch is the sourced QC procedure (R-0033); R-0005 forbids any batch adjustment here so the step only documents the confounding.

constraints: Probe every package before use (R: requireNamespace("DESeq2", quietly=TRUE); Python: import test) — the sandbox package inventory could not be read, so nothing may be assumed present. Degrade gracefully: if DESeq2 is absent, do the same QC on log2(CPM+1) with base R or with pandas/numpy/scipy/matplotlib, and say in the output which route was taken.
Use the variance stabilizing transformation with blind=TRUE (design-blind) for QC; if DESeq2 is unavailable use log2(CPM+1).
PCA on the top 500 most variable genes.

Do NOT apply any batch correction, ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or surrogate-variable method at this or any later step — batch is perfectly confounded with condition and any such removal deletes the condition effect (knowledge rule R-0005).
Print the condition x batch contingency table into the step output verbatim.
Save the sample-ordered filtered/unfiltered count matrix and the validated metadata as artifacts for the downstream steps.
steps.description: Load /eval-phase0-with-confounded-batch-n6-2/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, first column gene symbol) and /eval-phase0-with-confounded-batch-n6-2/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows x 3 columns: sample, condition, batch). Verify sample IDs match between the two files and reorder counts columns to metadata order. Cross-tabulate condition against batch and report the table explicitly — it is expected to be perfectly diagonal (B1 = 6 control, B2 = 6 treated), and the script must state in its output that condition and batch are the same partition of the samples and therefore not separable. Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~ condition, apply the variance stabilizing transformation blind to the design, compute PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and draw a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap. Colour/shape every plot by BOTH condition and batch, and state in the figure caption that the two annotations are identical by construction so the plots cannot attribute any axis to one factor over the other. Also report per-sample library sizes, the number of detected genes per sample, and flag any sample whose library size is far from the median or that sits away from its group.
acceptance_criteria: The condition x batch contingency table is reported and shows 6 control in B1 and 6 treated in B2, with an explicit statement that the two factors are aliased.
A PCA plot on the top 500 variable genes and a sample-distance heatmap exist, each annotated by condition and by batch.
Per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts are reported for all 12 samples, with any outlier named.
The output states which packages were actually available and which route was used.
No batch-corrected matrix is produced.

steps.name: DESeq2 treated vs control (confounded)
caveats: Nominal FDR control here is control over the treated-vs-control statistical contrast, not over a treatment effect. The gene list is a batch-plus-treatment list.
A large number of significant genes is exactly what a strong batch effect also produces — the count of DE genes is not evidence that the treatment worked.
At 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces count outliers, so some genes carry NA p-values by design; report them separately from filtered genes.
steps.context: 6 treated (all batch B2) vs 6 control (all batch B1), human lung, 12,000 gene symbols, salmon counts. Fixed-effects two-group design at 6 replicates per group is squarely in the range where the DESeq2 Wald test controls FDR. The batch term is deliberately omitted because ~ batch + condition is rank-deficient — this is not an oversight and the report must say so.
steps.question: Which genes differ between the 6 treated (batch B2) and the 6 control (batch B1) lung samples, under the unverifiable assumption that batch B1 and B2 introduced no expression difference?

grounding.reason: R-0005 fires: batch B1/B2 is perfectly confounded with control/treated, so the flag outcome confounded_label_or_stop is taken as 'label' — condition-only design, no batch term, no ComBat-seq/SVA/removeBatchEffect, and every result labelled confounded; the test itself is the DESeq2 Wald test with shrunken LFC, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and the minimal 10-counts-in-6-samples pre-filter per R-0001/R-0009/R-0010/R-0002.

constraints: Probe DESeq2 with requireNamespace before use. If DESeq2 is absent, fall back to edgeR quasi-likelihood as the primary test, or to a negative-binomial/limma-voom equivalent that is present, and state the substitution prominently. If no count-model package is available at all, report that the step could not run rather than substituting a t-test on raw counts silently.

Design formula is ~ condition. Do NOT add batch. Do NOT run ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, sva/svaseq, or RUV on these counts (knowledge rule R-0005: the model matrix is not full rank and removal would delete the condition effect).
Set the condition reference level explicitly to control; name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated, control).
Pre-filter: >=10 counts in >=6 samples. Do not filter harder — independent filtering in results() does the rest.
Keep independent filtering ON and pass alpha=0.05 to results(), the same cutoff used for reporting.
Select significant genes by padj only — never by raw p-value and never by fold change alone.
Keep both the unshrunken and the shrunken log2FC columns in the output table.
Every artifact (CSV header comment, figure title, summary text) must state: 'treated vs control is perfectly confounded with batch B2 vs B1; these differences cannot be attributed to treatment.'
steps.description: Primary differential expression on counts.csv with the metadata from T1S1. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~ condition ONLY, setting the reference level of condition explicitly to control so that a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Do not pre-normalize or pre-scale the counts — DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors go into the model as an offset. Run the Wald test, extract results for the contrast (condition, treated, control) with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering left ON, and adjust p-values by Benjamini-Hochberg. Report the shrunken log2 fold change beside the unshrunken MLE estimate in the same table (shrinkage for ranking and reporting of effect size; use the apeglm prior on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient, or ashr if apeglm is not installed — state which was used). Report separately (a) the number of genes tested after the pre-filter, (b) the number with padj < 0.05, (c) the number whose p-value is NA because DESeq2 flagged a Cook's-distance count outlier (at 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces), and (d) the number set to NA by independent filtering. Produce an MA plot, a volcano plot, a heatmap of the VST values for the top genes by padj, and the full results table as CSV sorted by padj. Every output file and every figure title must carry the label that this contrast is confounded with processing batch.
acceptance_criteria: A results table for the (condition, treated, control) contrast covering every tested gene, with baseMean, unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, sorted by padj.
Reported counts of: genes tested after the pre-filter, genes with padj < 0.05, genes NA from Cook's outlier flagging, genes NA from independent filtering.
The design formula used is recorded as ~ condition with control as reference, and no batch-adjusted matrix exists anywhere in the outputs.
MA plot, volcano plot and a top-gene VST heatmap are produced.
The confounding statement appears in the step summary and in the results-table header.

steps.name: edgeR QL cross-check and overlap
caveats: Concordance between DESeq2 and edgeR measures statistical robustness only. Both tools are fitting the same confounded contrast and will reproduce a batch effect equally faithfully.
If edgeR is not installed the step degrades to a no-op cross-check; that must be stated rather than silently skipped.
steps.context: At 6 biological replicates per group the two count-model tools agree on most genes but each calls some the other does not, and disagreement grows at low counts. The intersection is the defensible set to carry forward. The confounding with batch B1/B2 is unchanged by using a second method — agreement between two tools on the same aliased design does not de-confound anything.
steps.question: Which of the treated-vs-control genes are called by both the DESeq2 Wald test and the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same 12 lung samples?

grounding.reason: R-0042 asks for the DESeq2 / edgeR-QL overlap as the robustness check with the intersection as the high-confidence set and the union never reported; R-0001 names edgeR QL as the permitted second method at 6 replicates per group; R-0005 keeps the design condition-only here too.

constraints: Probe edgeR with requireNamespace before use. If edgeR is absent, report that the robustness cross-check could not be run and carry the DESeq2 result forward unchanged — do not invent a substitute test and call it a replication.
Use the same pre-filtered gene set and the same sample ordering as T1S2 so the two gene lists are directly comparable.
Model matrix ~ condition only, control as reference. No batch term, no batch correction.
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-specific calls as a secondary set; do NOT report the union as the finding.
Repeat the confounding label on all outputs of this step.
steps.description: Re-run the identical contrast with edgeR: same pre-filtered count matrix and same sample order from T1S1, TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp and glmQLFit on the model matrix ~ condition with control as reference, glmQLFTest for the treated-vs-control coefficient, and BH adjustment at FDR < 0.05. Then compare against the T1S2 DESeq2 result: report n significant by DESeq2, n significant by edgeR, and the size of the intersection; write out the intersection as the high-confidence gene set, and write the DESeq2-only and edgeR-only genes as a secondary set naming the method that called each. Produce a scatter of the DESeq2 shrunken log2FC against the edgeR log2FC over all tested genes with the Pearson and Spearman correlation, and a two-set Venn or an equivalent overlap table. Do not present the union as the result.
acceptance_criteria: n significant at FDR < 0.05 for DESeq2, for edgeR, and the intersection size are all reported.
The intersection gene set is written as a table, and the DESeq2-only / edgeR-only genes are written separately with the calling method named.
A log2FC concordance scatter with a reported correlation coefficient exists.
The union is not presented as the result anywhere.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on hallmark sets
caveats: Enrichment methods disagree with each other; a set here is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a finding.
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment of count data; using the tested genes as the universe and a ranked test mitigates but does not remove this.
With batch aliased to condition, an enriched pathway may be a signature of the processing run rather than of the treatment.
steps.context: No reference store is provisioned at planning time, so the hallmark collection may or may not exist when this runs. This step enriches the interpretation; the differential expression answer in T1S2/T1S3 stands without it. Human lung, 12,000 gene symbols, so the tested universe after filtering will be well under a full transcriptome and set intersections will be correspondingly small.
steps.question: Which biological processes are coordinately shifted between treated (B2) and control (B1) lung samples, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic?

grounding.reason: Human data, so hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways/GO (R-0048); preranked fgsea on the full tested list with tested genes as the universe and a 15-500 size window after intersection (R-0045/R-0046/R-0047), redundant sets collapsed (R-0052). Disputed ranking metric (R-0007): the DESeq2 Wald statistic is chosen because it is signed and scaled by its standard error, and the step states the choice.

constraints: Probe fgsea (or clusterProfiler as a fallback) with requireNamespace before use. If no GSEA package is importable, report that and stop — do not hand-roll an enrichment.

Resolve the gene set collection from the environment's reference data at run time. If NO human hallmark or pathway gene set collection is available, report that plainly, emit the ranked gene list as the artifact, and end the step successfully with the enrichment marked as not performed. Do not download anything and do not hard-code gene sets from memory.
Rank the FULL tested gene list; never cut it at padj or at a fold change before the test (knowledge rule R-0045).
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or annotation.
Gene set size window 15-500 applied AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes.
Collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per overlap group, with the full table kept as a supplement.
State the ranking-metric choice (Wald statistic) and that the enrichment result is method-dependent.
Repeat the confounding label: an enriched pathway here reflects a treated+B2 versus control+B1 contrast, so a batch-driven process would enrich identically.
steps.description: Preranked gene set enrichment on the FULL list of genes tested in T1S2 — not a thresholded list — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column). The ranking metric is a disputed choice among the Wald statistic, the signed -log10 p-value, and the shrunken log2FC; this plan chooses the Wald statistic because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, and the step must state that choice and that other metrics would reorder the list. Resolve a hallmark-style human gene set collection from whatever reference data the environment holds at run time; the required resource is a human hallmark pathway gene set collection keyed by gene symbol (the counts matrix uses gene symbols, so no ID mapping should be needed — verify the overlap between the ranked list and the set members and report it). Intersect each set with the tested genes and keep only sets with 15 to 500 members after that intersection. Run fgsea with BH adjustment, collapse redundant significant sets that share most of their members and report one representative per group with its leading-edge genes, and keep the full table as a supplement. If hallmark sets are present, follow up the leading hits against Reactome, WikiPathways or GO sets if those are also available. Report the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe (tested genes), the size window and the tool version alongside the results.
acceptance_criteria: A preranked GSEA table with NES, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge genes, or an explicit statement that no gene set collection was available with the ranked list emitted instead.
The number of ranked genes, the number of sets passing the 15-500 window after intersection, and the collection name/version are reported.
The ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic) and the universe (tested genes) are stated in the output.
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to representatives, with the full table retained.
The confounding caveat appears in the step summary.

steps.name: Confounding-aware synthesis report
caveats: The report cannot rescue the design; it can only make the limitation impossible to miss.
Effect sizes here are upper bounds on any treatment effect, since batch contributes to them in unknown proportion.
steps.context: This step produces the artifact a reader will act on, and its job is to prevent a confounded gene list from being read as a treatment signature. It computes nothing new.
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control lung expression from this 6-vs-6 design in which batch B2 holds every treated sample and batch B1 every control?

grounding.reason: R-0041 fixes the required reporting fields, R-0051 the enrichment provenance fields, R-0055 the method-dependence caveat, R-0042 the two-method overlap; R-0005 requires every result of this confounded design to be labelled as such, which this report carries as its lead.

constraints: Do not restate a DE gene as treatment-responsive without the confounding qualifier anywhere in the report.
Report package versions from the actual session, not from the plan.
Report NA p-value counts split by cause (outlier flag vs independent filtering).
Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set and never the union.
If T2S1 could not run for lack of gene sets, say so in the report rather than omitting the enrichment section.

State the remedy in terms of experimental design (batches spanning both conditions, or bridging technical replicates), and state explicitly that no statistical adjustment of these 12 samples can substitute for it.
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Lead with the design limitation: batch is perfectly confounded with condition, so no gene list from this dataset can be attributed to treatment, and the reported differences are treatment-plus-batch. Then give the reproducibility record required of any DE report: the method and version of each package actually used, the design formula (~ condition) and the named contrast (condition, treated, control), the pre-filter and the significance thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes at padj < 0.05, the number of NA p-values by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering), the DESeq2/edgeR intersection size, and the full session information. For the enrichment, record the gene set collection and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the tool version and the multiple-testing method, and state that enrichment results are method-dependent. Present the top genes of the high-confidence intersection as a table of candidate — not confirmed — treatment-responsive genes. Close with the concrete remedy: the comparison becomes interpretable only with samples where each processing batch contains both conditions (or with technical replicates of a subset of samples across B1 and B2 to estimate the batch shift); state that no reanalysis of these 12 samples can supply that.
acceptance_criteria: The report leads with the batch/condition confounding and its consequence for interpretation.
Method, package versions, design formula, named contrast, thresholds, n tested, n DE, NA counts by cause, and session info are all present.
The enrichment record names the collection and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window and the multiple-testing method, or states that enrichment was not performed.
A candidate gene table from the DESeq2/edgeR intersection is included, labelled as candidates under a confounded design.
A concrete design-level remedy is stated.

plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: 12,000 gene-symbol rows x 12 human lung samples of raw salmon-derived integer counts (counts.csv) with a 12 x 3 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying condition and batch. The design is 6 treated vs 6 control, and processing batch is PERFECTLY confounded with condition — batch B1 holds all 6 controls, batch B2 holds all 6 treated. This single fact governs the whole plan.

Because batch and condition are aliased, no statistical procedure can separate a treatment effect from a batch effect in this dataset. The model matrix for ~ batch + condition is rank-deficient, and ComBat-seq / removeBatchEffect / SVA-style adjustment would strip the condition effect along with the batch (Nygaard 2016; knowledge rule R-0005). The plan therefore fits condition only, and every downstream result is labelled as a confounded treated-vs-B2 / control-vs-B1 contrast rather than a treatment effect. T1S1 makes the confounding visible before any test: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, with the metadata cross-tabulated to demonstrate that condition and batch are the same partition. T1S2 runs the primary DESeq2 Wald test on ~ condition with control as the explicit reference level, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and shrunken effect sizes reported beside the raw MLE estimates. T1S3 repeats the same contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and reports the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042), since at 6 replicates per group the two tools agree on most but not all genes. T2S1 takes the full ranked gene list — never a thresholded one — into preranked GSEA against hallmark gene sets, with the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the chosen ranking metric (the ranking metric is a disputed choice; the Wald statistic is selected because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error). No reference store is provisioned right now, so T2S1 must resolve hallmark sets at run time and, if none are present, report that plainly and fall back to reporting the ranked list only — the enrichment enriches the answer but the research question survives without it. T2S2 assembles the reproducibility report: methods, package versions, design, thresholds, n tested, n DE, the two-method overlap, and the confounding statement that must accompany any gene list from this dataset.

The honest headline this plan is built to deliver: this experiment cannot establish which genes respond to treatment. It can only produce a ranked list of genes that differ between two groups that differ in both treatment and processing batch. Every artifact says so.

Run the Wald test, extract results for the contrast (condition, treated, control) with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering left ON, and adjust p-values by Benjamini-Hochberg. Report the shrunken log2 fold change beside the unshrunken MLE estimate in the same table (shrinkage for ranking and reporting of effect size; use the apeglm prior on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient, or ashr if apeglm is not installed — state which was used). Report separately (a) the number of genes tested after the pre-filter, (b) the number with padj < 0.05, (c) the number whose p-value is NA because DESeq2 flagged a Cook's-distance count outlier (at 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces), and (d) the number set to NA by independent filtering. Produce an MA plot, a volcano plot, a heatmap of the VST values for the top genes by padj, and the full results table as CSV sorted by padj. Every output file and every figure title must carry the label that this contrast is confounded with processing batch.
steps.context: 6 treated (all batch B2) vs 6 control (all batch B1), human lung, 12,000 gene symbols, salmon counts. Fixed-effects two-group design at 6 replicates per group is squarely in the range where the DESeq2 Wald test controls FDR. The batch term is deliberately omitted because ~ batch + condition is rank-deficient — this is not an oversight and the report must say so.
constraints: Probe DESeq2 with requireNamespace before use. If DESeq2 is absent, fall back to edgeR quasi-likelihood as the primary test, or to a negative-binomial/limma-voom equivalent that is present, and state the substitution prominently. If no count-model package is available at all, report that the step could not run rather than substituting a t-test on raw counts silently.

Design formula is ~ condition. Do NOT add batch. Do NOT run ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, sva/svaseq, or RUV on these counts (knowledge rule R-0005: the model matrix is not full rank and removal would delete the condition effect).
Set the condition reference level explicitly to control; name the contrast as the triple (condition, treated, control).
Pre-filter: >=10 counts in >=6 samples. Do not filter harder — independent filtering in results() does the rest.
Keep independent filtering ON and pass alpha=0.05 to results(), the same cutoff used for reporting.
Select significant genes by padj only — never by raw p-value and never by fold change alone.
Keep both the unshrunken and the shrunken log2FC columns in the output table.
Every artifact (CSV header comment, figure title, summary text) must state: 'treated vs control is perfectly confounded with batch B2 vs B1; these differences cannot be attributed to treatment.'
acceptance_criteria: A results table for the (condition, treated, control) contrast covering every tested gene, with baseMean, unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, sorted by padj.
Reported counts of: genes tested after the pre-filter, genes with padj < 0.05, genes NA from Cook's outlier flagging, genes NA from independent filtering.
The design formula used is recorded as ~ condition with control as reference, and no batch-adjusted matrix exists anywhere in the outputs.
MA plot, volcano plot and a top-gene VST heatmap are produced.
The confounding statement appears in the step summary and in the results-table header.
caveats: Nominal FDR control here is control over the treated-vs-control statistical contrast, not over a treatment effect. The gene list is a batch-plus-treatment list.
A large number of significant genes is exactly what a strong batch effect also produces — the count of DE genes is not evidence that the treatment worked.
At 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces count outliers, so some genes carry NA p-values by design; report them separately from filtered genes.

grounding.reason: R-0005 fires: batch B1/B2 is perfectly confounded with control/treated, so the flag outcome confounded_label_or_stop is taken as 'label' — condition-only design, no batch term, no ComBat-seq/SVA/removeBatchEffect, and every result labelled confounded; the test itself is the DESeq2 Wald test with shrunken LFC, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and the minimal 10-counts-in-6-samples pre-filter per R-0001/R-0009/R-0010/R-0002.

steps.name: edgeR QL cross-check and overlap
steps.question: Which of the treated-vs-control genes are called by both the DESeq2 Wald test and the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same 12 lung samples?
steps.description: Re-run the identical contrast with edgeR: same pre-filtered count matrix and same sample order from T1S1, TMM normalization factors, estimateDisp and glmQLFit on the model matrix ~ condition with control as reference, glmQLFTest for the treated-vs-control coefficient, and BH adjustment at FDR < 0.05. Then compare against the T1S2 DESeq2 result: report n significant by DESeq2, n significant by edgeR, and the size of the intersection; write out the intersection as the high-confidence gene set, and write the DESeq2-only and edgeR-only genes as a secondary set naming the method that called each. Produce a scatter of the DESeq2 shrunken log2FC against the edgeR log2FC over all tested genes with the Pearson and Spearman correlation, and a two-set Venn or an equivalent overlap table. Do not present the union as the result.
steps.context: At 6 biological replicates per group the two count-model tools agree on most genes but each calls some the other does not, and disagreement grows at low counts. The intersection is the defensible set to carry forward. The confounding with batch B1/B2 is unchanged by using a second method — agreement between two tools on the same aliased design does not de-confound anything.
constraints: Probe edgeR with requireNamespace before use. If edgeR is absent, report that the robustness cross-check could not be run and carry the DESeq2 result forward unchanged — do not invent a substitute test and call it a replication.
Use the same pre-filtered gene set and the same sample ordering as T1S2 so the two gene lists are directly comparable.
Model matrix ~ condition only, control as reference. No batch term, no batch correction.
Report the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-specific calls as a secondary set; do NOT report the union as the finding.
Repeat the confounding label on all outputs of this step.
acceptance_criteria: n significant at FDR < 0.05 for DESeq2, for edgeR, and the intersection size are all reported.
The intersection gene set is written as a table, and the DESeq2-only / edgeR-only genes are written separately with the calling method named.
A log2FC concordance scatter with a reported correlation coefficient exists.
The union is not presented as the result anywhere.
caveats: Concordance between DESeq2 and edgeR measures statistical robustness only. Both tools are fitting the same confounded contrast and will reproduce a batch effect equally faithfully.
If edgeR is not installed the step degrades to a no-op cross-check; that must be stated rather than silently skipped.

grounding.reason: R-0042 asks for the DESeq2 / edgeR-QL overlap as the robustness check with the intersection as the high-confidence set and the union never reported; R-0001 names edgeR QL as the permitted second method at 6 replicates per group; R-0005 keeps the design condition-only here too.

steps.name: Preranked GSEA on hallmark sets
steps.question: Which biological processes are coordinately shifted between treated (B2) and control (B1) lung samples, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic?
steps.description: Preranked gene set enrichment on the FULL list of genes tested in T1S2 — not a thresholded list — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column). The ranking metric is a disputed choice among the Wald statistic, the signed -log10 p-value, and the shrunken log2FC; this plan chooses the Wald statistic because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error, and the step must state that choice and that other metrics would reorder the list. Resolve a hallmark-style human gene set collection from whatever reference data the environment holds at run time; the required resource is a human hallmark pathway gene set collection keyed by gene symbol (the counts matrix uses gene symbols, so no ID mapping should be needed — verify the overlap between the ranked list and the set members and report it). Intersect each set with the tested genes and keep only sets with 15 to 500 members after that intersection. Run fgsea with BH adjustment, collapse redundant significant sets that share most of their members and report one representative per group with its leading-edge genes, and keep the full table as a supplement. If hallmark sets are present, follow up the leading hits against Reactome, WikiPathways or GO sets if those are also available. Report the collection name and version, the ranking metric, the universe (tested genes), the size window and the tool version alongside the results.
steps.context: No reference store is provisioned at planning time, so the hallmark collection may or may not exist when this runs. This step enriches the interpretation; the differential expression answer in T1S2/T1S3 stands without it. Human lung, 12,000 gene symbols, so the tested universe after filtering will be well under a full transcriptome and set intersections will be correspondingly small.
constraints: Probe fgsea (or clusterProfiler as a fallback) with requireNamespace before use. If no GSEA package is importable, report that and stop — do not hand-roll an enrichment.

Resolve the gene set collection from the environment's reference data at run time. If NO human hallmark or pathway gene set collection is available, report that plainly, emit the ranked gene list as the artifact, and end the step successfully with the enrichment marked as not performed. Do not download anything and do not hard-code gene sets from memory.
Rank the FULL tested gene list; never cut it at padj or at a fold change before the test (knowledge rule R-0045).
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or annotation.
Gene set size window 15-500 applied AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes.
Collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per overlap group, with the full table kept as a supplement.
State the ranking-metric choice (Wald statistic) and that the enrichment result is method-dependent.
Repeat the confounding label: an enriched pathway here reflects a treated+B2 versus control+B1 contrast, so a batch-driven process would enrich identically.
acceptance_criteria: A preranked GSEA table with NES, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge genes, or an explicit statement that no gene set collection was available with the ranked list emitted instead.
The number of ranked genes, the number of sets passing the 15-500 window after intersection, and the collection name/version are reported.
The ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic) and the universe (tested genes) are stated in the output.
Redundant significant sets are collapsed to representatives, with the full table retained.
The confounding caveat appears in the step summary.
caveats: Enrichment methods disagree with each other; a set here is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a finding.
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment of count data; using the tested genes as the universe and a ranked test mitigates but does not remove this.
With batch aliased to condition, an enriched pathway may be a signature of the processing run rather than of the treatment.

grounding.reason: Human data, so hallmark first then Reactome/WikiPathways/GO (R-0048); preranked fgsea on the full tested list with tested genes as the universe and a 15-500 size window after intersection (R-0045/R-0046/R-0047), redundant sets collapsed (R-0052). Disputed ranking metric (R-0007): the DESeq2 Wald statistic is chosen because it is signed and scaled by its standard error, and the step states the choice.

steps.name: Confounding-aware synthesis report
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control lung expression from this 6-vs-6 design in which batch B2 holds every treated sample and batch B1 every control?
steps.description: Assemble the final report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. Lead with the design limitation: batch is perfectly confounded with condition, so no gene list from this dataset can be attributed to treatment, and the reported differences are treatment-plus-batch. Then give the reproducibility record required of any DE report: the method and version of each package actually used, the design formula (~ condition) and the named contrast (condition, treated, control), the pre-filter and the significance thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes at padj < 0.05, the number of NA p-values by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering), the DESeq2/edgeR intersection size, and the full session information. For the enrichment, record the gene set collection and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window, the tool version and the multiple-testing method, and state that enrichment results are method-dependent. Present the top genes of the high-confidence intersection as a table of candidate — not confirmed — treatment-responsive genes. Close with the concrete remedy: the comparison becomes interpretable only with samples where each processing batch contains both conditions (or with technical replicates of a subset of samples across B1 and B2 to estimate the batch shift); state that no reanalysis of these 12 samples can supply that.
steps.context: This step produces the artifact a reader will act on, and its job is to prevent a confounded gene list from being read as a treatment signature. It computes nothing new.
constraints: Do not restate a DE gene as treatment-responsive without the confounding qualifier anywhere in the report.
Report package versions from the actual session, not from the plan.
Report NA p-value counts split by cause (outlier flag vs independent filtering).
Report the DESeq2/edgeR intersection as the high-confidence set and never the union.
If T2S1 could not run for lack of gene sets, say so in the report rather than omitting the enrichment section.

State the remedy in terms of experimental design (batches spanning both conditions, or bridging technical replicates), and state explicitly that no statistical adjustment of these 12 samples can substitute for it.
acceptance_criteria: The report leads with the batch/condition confounding and its consequence for interpretation.
Method, package versions, design formula, named contrast, thresholds, n tested, n DE, NA counts by cause, and session info are all present.
The enrichment record names the collection and version, the ranking metric, the universe, the size window and the multiple-testing method, or states that enrichment was not performed.
A candidate gene table from the DESeq2/edgeR intersection is included, labelled as candidates under a confounded design.
A concrete design-level remedy is stated.
caveats: The report cannot rescue the design; it can only make the limitation impossible to miss.
Effect sizes here are upper bounds on any treatment effect, since batch contributes to them in unknown proportion.

grounding.reason: R-0041 fixes the required reporting fields, R-0051 the enrichment provenance fields, R-0055 the method-dependence caveat, R-0042 the two-method overlap; R-0005 requires every result of this confounded design to be labelled as such, which this report carries as its lead.
